1.title: Transmission Media, Transceivers and Topologies
1.text: Welcome to Module five: Transmission Media, Transceivers and Topologies. It covers the exam area one point zero Networking Concepts. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. one point five Compare and contrast transmission media and transceivers (wireless eight oh two dot eleven, cellular, satellite. Wired eight oh two dot three, single-mode and multimode fiber, direct attach copper, coaxial, cable speeds, plenum. Ethernet and Fibre Channel transceivers, S F P and Q S F P. Connector types). one point six Compare and contrast network topologies, architectures and types (mesh, hybrid, star, spine and leaf, point to point, three-tier hierarchy, collapsed core, north-south and east-west traffic flows). Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: one point zero Networking Concepts (twenty-three percent). Exam format: up to ninety questions in ninety minutes; a score of seven hundred twenty on a scale of one hundred to nine hundred passes. Validated against: the official Comp T I A Network plus N ten to nine exam objectives, version four point zero.

1.title: Wired and wireless media
1.text: Wired and wireless media. Twisted pair copper (eight oh two dot three). Cat five E: one gigabit per second to one hundred m; Cat six: one gigabit per second (ten gigabits per second to about fifty-five m); Cat six A: ten gigabits per second to one hundred m; Cat seven shielded; Cat eight: twenty-five or forty gigabits per second to about thirty m. U T P unshielded, S T P shielded (less interference). Single-mode fiber (S M F). One light path, laser, long distances (kilometers). Multimode fiber (M M F). Many light paths, L E D or V C S E L, shorter distances (hundreds of meters), cheaper optics.

1.title: Wired and wireless media, continued
1.text: Wired and wireless media. Direct attach copper (D A C) or twinaxial. Pre-terminated copper cable with transceivers built in, very short (a few meters), between racks or devices. Coaxial. Cable T V and broadband; F-type connectors. Wireless eight oh two dot eleven. Wi-Fi (Module ten). Cellular. W A N access over mobile networks (four G or five G). Satellite. Remote areas, high latency. Plenum cable has fire-retardant, low-smoke jacket and must be used in air-handling spaces (above ceilings, in ducts); non-plenum (P V C) is cheaper and not for plenum spaces. Exam tip: Long distance equals single-mode fiber. Short, cheap server links between racks equals D A C. Cable in a ceiling air space equals plenum rated.

1.title: Transceivers and connectors
1.text: Transceivers and connectors. S F P (small form-factor pluggable). Hot-swappable module for one gigabit per second (S F P plus for ten gigabits per second). Q S F P (quad S F P). Four lanes, forty gigabits per second and higher (Q S F P plus, Q S F P twenty-eight). Protocols. Ethernet or Fibre Channel (F C) for storage; the transceiver must match the protocol, fiber type and speed.

1.title: Transceivers and connectors, continued
1.text: Transceivers and connectors. The figure shows this: Common connector types: R J eleven, R J forty-five, F-type, B N C, S C, L C, S T and M P O.

1.title: Transceivers and connectors, continued
1.text: Transceivers and connectors. R J eleven. Telephone (two pairs). R J forty-five. Ethernet twisted pair. F-type. Coaxial (cable T V, broadband). B N C. Coaxial, older networks and video. S C (subscriber connector). Fiber, square push-pull. L C (local connector). Fiber, small, most common on S F P. S T (straight tip). Fiber, round twist-lock. M P O (multi-fiber push on). Fiber, many fibers in one connector (Q S F P).

1.title: Topologies and architectures
1.text: Topologies and architectures. Mesh. Devices connect to many others; redundant, costly (full or partial mesh). Star or hub and spoke. Devices connect to a central point; single point of failure at the center. Hybrid. A mix of topologies. Point to point. A dedicated link between two sites. Spine and leaf. Data center design: every leaf switch connects to every spine switch; predictable low latency, east-west traffic. Three-tier hierarchical. Core (fast backbone), distribution (policy, routing between V L A Ns), access (end devices). Collapsed core. Core and distribution combined in one layer (smaller sites).

1.title: Topologies and architectures, continued
1.text: Topologies and architectures. North-south. Between clients outside and servers in the data center. East-west. Between servers inside the data center. Exam tip: Match the transceiver, fiber type and speed at both ends; a single-mode optic does not work on multimode fiber.

1.title: Topologies and architectures, continued
1.text: Topologies and architectures. The figure shows this: Three-tier hierarchy compared with spine and leaf. Exam tip: Lots of server-to-server traffic equals spine and leaf (east-west). Campus with core, distribution and access equals three-tier. Smaller site equals collapsed core.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A link must span fifteen kilometers between two buildings. Which medium fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Single-mode fiber. Single-mode fiber supports very long distances.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Which cable type must be installed above a drop ceiling used as an air-return space? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Plenum-rated cable. Plenum cable has a fire-retardant, low-smoke jacket for air-handling spaces.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A data center has heavy server-to-server traffic and needs predictable latency. Which design fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Spine and leaf. Spine and leaf is built for east-west traffic.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which fiber connector is small, push-pull, and common on S F P modules? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: L C. L C is the small connector used on most S F Ps.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Two switches in adjacent racks must be linked cheaply over two meters at ten gigabits per second. What fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A direct attach copper cable. D A C is a short, inexpensive pre-terminated link.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which layer of the three-tier model provides the high-speed backbone? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Core. The core is the fast backbone.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which Cat standard supports ten gigabits per second to one hundred meters? Answer: Cat six A. Question two. What is the difference between S M F and M M F? Answer: Single-mode uses one light path for long distance; multimode uses many paths for shorter distance. Question three. What does S F P stand for? Answer: Small form-factor pluggable.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which connector is used for Ethernet twisted pair? Answer: R J forty-five. Question five. What is east-west traffic? Answer: Traffic between servers inside the data center. Question six. What is a collapsed core? Answer: Core and distribution layers combined in one.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Copper: Cat five E or six one gigabit per second, Cat six A ten gigabits per second one hundred m, Cat eight short. Fiber: S M F long distance (laser), M M F short; D A C for short links. Transceivers: S F P (one gigabit per second), Q S F P (forty gigabits per second plus ); Ethernet versus Fibre Channel. Connectors: R J forty-five, R J eleven, F-type, B N C, S C, L C, S T, M P O. Topologies: mesh, star, hybrid, point to point, spine and leaf, three-tier, collapsed core.
